title: Career Roadmap · Agri Assistant
summary: An Agricultural Assistant supports crop production, field demonstrations, soil and crop monitoring, farmer guidance, pest-management awareness and implementation of agricultural development programmes.

facts.Current degree: Diploma in Agriculture, Horticulture or a relevant agricultural qualification, depending on the post

blocks.label: Recommended stream
blocks.text: Science with Biology or Agriculture, where available; accepted streams depend on the course.

blocks.label: Important subjects
blocks.text: Biology, chemistry, agriculture, soil science and mathematics.

blocks.label: Admission
blocks.text: Diploma and degree entry requirements vary by state and institution.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Crop production, irrigation, soil health, horticulture and sustainable farming.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Field observation, recordkeeping, communication and basic computer use.

items.text: Diploma in Agriculture → Agricultural field support, farm operations and eligible assistant posts.
Diploma in Horticulture → Fruit, vegetable, nursery and ornamental crop support.
Diploma in Sericulture → Silkworm rearing and silk-production support.
B.Sc. Agriculture → Broader agricultural extension, technical and postgraduate opportunities.
B.Sc. Horticulture → Horticultural production, nursery management and related technical roles.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: Government recruitment posts titled Agricultural Assistant, Agriculture Extension Officer or similar may require specific qualifications, subjects, age criteria and selection tests. A diploma is not automatically accepted for every post.

ICAR

blocks.label: Year 1
blocks.text: Crop science, soil basics, agricultural tools, farm records and communication.

blocks.label: Year 2
blocks.text: Crop management, irrigation, pest identification, farmer outreach and field demonstrations.

blocks.label: Year 3, if applicable
blocks.text: Advanced fieldwork, internships, project work and recruitment preparation.

blocks.label: Final stage
blocks.text: Build practical experience and prepare for eligible government or private-sector vacancies.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Soil-health recordbook • Crop pest-observation log • Demonstration plot • Farmer advisory leaflet on water-efficient irrigation.

blocks.label: Government / research
blocks.text: Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), agricultural universities, state agriculture departments and research farms.

blocks.label: Private
blocks.text: Seed companies, fertiliser firms, crop-protection companies, agri-tech startups and farm-input dealers.

blocks.label: Ideal exposure
blocks.text: Crop monitoring, soil sampling, farmer training, nursery operations and agricultural data collection.
Internship availability depends on the institution and employer; field placements are not guaranteed.

blocks.label: Common requirements
blocks.text: Academic transcripts, relevant prerequisites, English proficiency where required, proof of funding and student-visa documentation. Diploma credit transfer depends on the university and programme.

blocks.label: Roles
blocks.text: Agricultural Field Technician, Farm Assistant, Crop Scout, Horticulture Technician, Research Field Assistant.

blocks.label: Industries
blocks.text: Commercial farms, horticulture, seeds, crop science, agricultural research and agri-tech.
Direct employment depends on local experience requirements, language, qualification recognition and visa rules. Sponsorship is not guaranteed.

Agriculture Student ↓ Field Trainee ↓ Agri Assistant / Field Assistant ↓ Experienced Agriculture Technician ↓ Senior Field Executive / Farm Supervisor ↓ Extension Coordinator / Technical Specialist ↓ Agriculture Project Manager / Entrepreneur
